To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the N-helical extension and cysteines in human voltage-dependent anion channels are functionally interdependent and that these residues are critical for channel function and biochemical stability.
the N-terminal helix and cysteines inter-regulate the function and stability of human mitochondrial VDAC-2.

the N-terminal extension (NTE, residues 2-12) of the N-terminal helix of hVDAC2 (residues 1-21) is required for its unique functional properties, including the highest cysteines content and thermodynamic stability among VDAC isoforms, and its unique voltage-gating properties, and the N-helix itself is required for channel activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the unique features of hVDAC2, and its interdependence on the N-helix, NTE and cysteines for function.
the functional interplay of the N-helical extension, cysteines and the membrane environment on the overall stability and function of hVDAC2.
the functional role of the NTE in hVDAC2 and how the cysteines influence its function and stability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N-helical domain of hVDAC2 plays a critical role in channel activity, while the NTE domain plays an important role in channel stability and regulation.
the NTE is a crucial determinant of hVDAC stability, function, and biochemistry.
hVDAC-1 is a channel with a higher conductance than hVDAC-3, but a lower stability, whereas the opposite is true for hVDAC- 2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the N-helices of VDACs are crucial for voltage gating and channel function, and that the NTE and cysteine content of hVDACs are important determinants for the overall stability and functional properties of this isoform.
hVDAC-1 and hVDAC-3 are more thermodynamically stable than hVDAC- 2, but the latter is more functionally active and is the most sensitive to voltage gating.
the N-helical extension in hVDAC2, which is absent in all other isoforms, is a key determinant for its unique functional characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NTE and cysteines are critical for hVDAC- 2 function, and their interplay is essential for its unique role in the outer membrane of human mitochondria.
hVDAC- 2, in contrast to other VDAC isoforms, is a highly dynamic protein that is sensitive to the local environment.
hVDAC-1/3 are not functionally equivalent to hVDAC- 2, and the latter isoform may be a more suitable target for therapeutic intervention.
